## Context
The A6-0b live deployment preflight and final receipt found two pre-existing untracked event JSONs in the persistent review-bot tickets clone while HEAD exactly equalled refs/remotes/origin/tickets:

- 172e-b207-4c18-4243/1785522649620648380-d92b157f-3a3e-4c66-85d9-b5f2ec06499e-TICKET_DIGEST.json
- 7ab3-9df0-7a90-4ffd/1785820923597137671-b00b8061-e68a-4ab1-8f13-0625c90da09e-CLAIM_ENRICH.json

They predate the A6-0b deployment. Ref convergence is healthy and there is no tracked diff, merge, rebase, or stash state, but a history rewrite/reset could overwrite or strand these uncommitted artifacts. Do not delete or raw-commit them without determining whether they are unique canonical events or duplicates.

## Plan
- Inspect only event identity/type/authorship metadata and compare each event UUID/path with the authoritative tickets branch.
- Determine whether each artifact is unique recoverable data, a duplicate of a committed event, or disposable failed-write residue.
- Recover unique events through the normal signed store write path, or record evidence supporting explicit deletion if duplicate/disposable.
- Re-run clone integrity/ref-convergence checks and prove the persistent clone has no untracked event files before the A6-1 publication window.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] [operator-attested] Each stranded path has a documented identity/duplication determination against authoritative origin/tickets.
- [x] [operator-attested] Any unique event is recovered through a normal signed store operation, or explicit operator evidence authorizes discarding a duplicate/disposable file.
- [x] [operator-attested] Persistent review-bot clone HEAD equals refs/remotes/origin/tickets with no tracked or untracked event files, merge, rebase, or stash state.
- [x] [operator-attested] The final clean-clone receipt is recorded before the A6-1 reclaim publication window.

No production source change is presumed; if investigation finds a reproducible writer defect, file a separate code bug with the reproduction.

## Verification
- Use read-only `git ls-tree`, `git log --all -- <path>`, and event-UUID search against `refs/remotes/origin/tickets` to classify each file.
- After the authorized recovery/discard operation, record `git status --short --untracked-files=all`, exact HEAD and origin/tickets tips, and absence of MERGE_HEAD, rebase directories, and stashes.
- Capture commands and exits through SSM without printing repository credentials.
